findings.finding: The 10-Q shows Q2's record $23.2m revenue included $8.5m recognised upfront from a $10m Curiosity Brands content license paid in four $2.5m annual instalments starting 2027-06-30, plus $5.3m of trade/barter license fees (vs $1.9m a year earlier); ex the Curiosity Brands license Q2 licensing was ~$5.6m, in line with Q1's ~$6.0m, and remaining performance obligations expected in the rest of 2026 are only $1.9m. The $20.3m Q3 consensus implies ~$11m of licensing with subscriptions flat near $8.9m, i.e. roughly double the ex-one-off run rate, so Q3 and the H2 $38-41m guide need another large deal or more barter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Licensing is the line this stock trades on: Q2 2026 licensing surprise +42.5% (2026-08-12), then fully faded to ~$2.55 by 2026-08-27 per the CEO's Form 4 purchase prices; Q1 2026 flat revenue and weak EBITDA -19.5% (2026-05-14); Q3 2025 +23.9% after a pre-print licensing PR (2025-10-29).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock gave back the whole Q2 pop and sits at a 52-week low, which is what pricing this would look like. What is not priced is the sell-side bar: the three Buy-rated analysts still hold FY at $78.75-79.25m (upper half of guide) and Q3 at $20.3m, which would not be the case if they had netted out the non-cash $8.5m license and the thin RPO. A miss against an unrevised bar plus a guide cut is the downside path.
findings.independence: The finviz preview (https://finviz.com/news/414864/curiositystream-must-prove-ai-licensing-boom-can-repeat-as-shares-sit-near-lows, 2026-11-03) independently computes the ~$11m licensing implied by consensus and quotes management that H2 licensing is lumpy and partly uncontracted; the panabee summary of the 10-Q (https://www.panabee.com/news/curiositystream-earnings-q3-2026) flags the $5.3m barter and $8.5m instalment license. Both rest on the same 10-Q.

findings.finding: Q4 dividend declaration, expected with tonight's release (Q3's $0.085/share, ~$5.0m, was declared with Q2 results on 2026-08-11), faces a funding question: cash was $5.4m at 2026-06-30 ($10.8m with investments), H1 operating cash flow was -$3.0m against $9.9m of dividends paid, the 10-Q says the Q3 dividend would be funded from cash, operating cash flow 'and possibly credit facility drawdowns', the Citibank revolver restricts dividends unless liquidity is at least $10m after payment, and Q3 also carried the $2.0m Spiegel buyout. At $2.375 the $0.34 annual dividend yields 14.3%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The dividend was raised from $0.05 to $0.085 with Q1 2026 results, which fell -19.5% on the operating line; no print has carried a dividend cut, so there is no reaction history on a cut.
findings.why_not_priced: A 14.3% yield is the market already pricing a cut or doubt about it, so a reduction is largely priced; a suspension, a revolver draw to fund it, or a cut to the year-end $17-22m cash guide would not be. If it were fully priced in the other direction (a maintained dividend expected), the stock would not trade at a 14% yield near its 52-week low.
findings.independence: The same 10-Q; panabee's 10-Q summary makes the same point about dividends exceeding operating cash flow (https://www.panabee.com/news/curiositystream-earnings-q3-2026). Financing question asked: the revolver money would fund a dividend, not a corroborated ramp, so the sign stays negative but small; an offsetting read is that a board maintaining the payout signals confidence in Q4 collections.

findings.finding: Q3 includes a remeasurement gain on the previously held 32% Spiegel Venture stake (zero carrying value) on the 2026-07-01 buyout of the remaining 68% for $2.0m, plus consolidation of the German business (pro forma adds ~$0.4m a quarter to revenue: Q2 $23.6m pro forma vs $23.2m reported) and accretion interest on the Curiosity Brands receivable from Q3; these lift GAAP EPS against a ~$0.03 consensus that may not include the gain.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None on below-the-line items; Q2's record GAAP net income of $8.9m (also flattered by a one-off) bought +42.5% and then faded entirely within two weeks.
findings.why_not_priced: A GAAP EPS beat driven by a remeasurement gain would show as a headline beat on aggregators; a stock this beaten down could pop on the headline in after-hours before the call. Sized as a one-off with no path to the guide.
findings.independence: Same 10-Q (subsequent events note); the Spiegel buyout was also announced in a 2026-07-07 8-K/press release (https://www.newswire.com/news/curiositystream-acquires-full-ownership-of-its-german-operations-strengthening).

findings.finding: Management guided an 18-20% cut in second-half operating expenses, which supports the H2 adj. EBITDA guide of $6-10m even if licensing is light; opex already fell 24.1% year over year in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 EBITDA of $11.4m vs $3.0m bought +42.5%; Q1 2026 EBITDA $0.9m was sold -19.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: It sits inside what the company already guided, so it is largely priced; it matters only as a floor under the EBITDA line if revenue misses.
findings.independence: Q2 press release shows opex down $4.5m (24.1%) y/y (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001776909/000162828026056318/pressrelease2q26qcuri-2026.htm).

findings.finding: CEO Clint Stinchcomb bought 50,000 shares in the open market on 2026-08-27/28 at weighted averages of $2.553 and $2.603 (~$130k), taking his direct holding to 3,021,260 shares, after the Q2 pop had faded and with the 10-Q already public; the stock is now ~7% below his purchase price.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior CEO open-market purchase found in the baseline window to compare against.
findings.why_not_priced: Form 4s on a three-analyst microcap are not on the wire; the purchase was made by the person who knows the Q3 licensing pipeline after the one-off nature of the Q2 license was disclosed. If the market had weighted it, the stock would not have fallen a further ~7% below his cost into the print.
findings.independence: Second Form 4 for the 2026-08-27 lot (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1776909/000162828026059526/xslF345X06/wk-form4_1788198076.xml). Same insider, so one finding.

findings.finding: CFO Brady Hayden stepped down effective 2026-09-01, two weeks after the record quarter (8-K says no disagreement), and filed Form 144s on 2026-09-03 to sell 105,931 shares (~$309k, ~$2.92) including shares bought on the open market in 2024; the replacement CFO, ex-EY partner Sean Piche, starts on a $120,000 annualised salary rising to $180,000 in 2027 with 150,000 inducement RSUs and held no shares, and the first quarter he signs is this one.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None; first CFO change in the baseline window.
findings.why_not_priced: The departure is public but the immediate sale of the former CFO's whole open-market lot and the low new-CFO salary sit in filings no aggregator reports; a new CFO's first quarter is where conservative accounting choices (barter recognition, receivable reserves, guide framing) tend to appear.
findings.independence: Form 144s: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1776909/000195917326006695/xsl144X01/primary_doc.xml and https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1776909/000193894026000002/xsl144X01/primary_doc.xml (2026-09-03). A former officer selling after leaving is also ordinary, which is why this is small.

baseline_tension: No skew read exists and options OI is call-heavy; the documented negative (one-off-inflated Q2, thin RPO, dividend funding) agrees with the run-up and the 52-week-low price, so much of it is likely priced, which is why p_up is only 45 and not lower.
lessons_applied: Rule 8 and 'documents beat inference': licensing run-rate finding rests on a 10-Q revenue/RPO walk on a three-analyst name, enlarged from -3.0 to -3.5 (kept below the median reaction because the 10-Q has been public since August and the stock has fallen with it).
Rule 4 and 'covenant arithmetic did not pay': dividend-funding finding shrunk from -1.5 to -1.0; financing question answered (revolver would fund a dividend, not a ramp), so the sign stays negative.
Rule 2: Spiegel remeasurement gain is a one-off with no path to the guide, shrunk from +0.5 to +0.2.
Rule 6: H2 opex cut lands inside the company's own guide, shrunk from +0.3 to +0.1.
Rule 5: unexplained drawdown worth 0 and absence is not a cause: positioning finding shrunk from +1.0 to +0.3 (only the short-covering fact kept), no-pre-print-PR finding from -0.5 to -0.2.
Rule 7: short interest checked before the negatives (3.5%, 4 days, falling): not crowded, negatives not shrunk for squeeze risk.
